classification.difficultyReason: Use equal side lengths to form two simultaneous equations, solve by substitution and interpret the side length.

content.prompt: Find the length of the sides of the equilateral triangle.

spec.description: Unshaded equilateral triangle with an upper apex and horizontal base; no vertex names, markers or equality ticks. Source blue outlines become ordinary black outlines under house style.
spec.mathematics: Left side 3y-x; right side 2+2y; base 5x+3. All three sides are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied side expressions are visible in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal.
$$\begin{align*}
3y-x &= 2+2y \\
y-x &= 2 \qquad (1) \\
3y-x &= 5x+3 \\
3y-6x &= 3 \qquad (2)
\end{align*}$$
From (1), $y=x+2$. Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}
3(x+2)-6x &= 3 \\
3x+6-6x &= 3 \\
-3x &= -3 \\
x &= 1 \\
y &= 1+2 \\
y &= 3
\end{align*}$$
Each side has length $5(1)+3=8$ units.
